newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. condemns attacks on peacekeepers in Georgia.
newsitem.headline: U.N. condemns attacks on peacekeepers in Georgia.

text.p: Security Council members on Tuesday condemned attacks on convoys belonging to peacekeepers of the Russian-led Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) in Georgia's breakaway Abkhazia region.

A statement read to reporters by council president Njuguna Mahugu of Kenya after consultations on a number of topics referred particularly to an attack on an ambulance last Saturday in which a nurse and two soldiers were killed.
"The members of the Security Council...strongly condemned the attacks by remote-controlled mines on the convoys of collective peacekeeping forces of the CIS," he said.

"The members of the council also stressed the inadmissibility of those acts in contravention of the Geneva Convention and the Moscow agreement of May 14, 1994 on a ceasefire and separation of forces."
They condemned the continued laying of mines in the Gali region, near the border with the breakaway region.

The council members also called on the parties to take all measures to prevent any terrorist acts and to cooperate fully with U.N. observers and the CIS peacekeeping force, and to honour their commitments to ensure the safety and freedom of movement of all international personnel.
Abkhaz irregulars ousted Georgian troops in 1993 after a year-long conflict in which over 10,000 people were killed and some 250,000 Georgians fled the region.

The 2,500-strong CIS force and a U.N. mission are sanctioned by the Georgian government and the Abkhaz leadership. But some Georgians, especially among refugees who fled Abkhazia, oppose the Russian involvement and want to retake the region by force.
